question: Your Claude Agent SDK agent automates a repetitive task: it runs a project's test suite and investigates any failures. In one run, Claude requested Bash to run the tests. On the next iteration, it requested Grep with the exact name of the function that had failed. A new engineer asks how Claude knew which name to search for. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The loop appended the Bash output to the conversation history as a tool result, so the next request included the failing function name.
options.reason: The guide says tool results are appended to the conversation history so the model can reason about the next action with the new information.

options.text: A rule in the agent definition always runs Grep after Bash and copies the failing function name from the test output into the search.
options.reason: The guide contrasts model-driven decisions, where Claude reasons about the next tool from context, with pre-configured tool sequences. Here Claude itself requested Grep.

options.text: Claude returned stop_reason "end_turn" after the test run, and the loop then sent a fresh request asking Claude to search the codebase.
options.reason: The guide says Claude requests a tool with stop_reason "tool_use", and "end_turn" ends the loop. A fresh request without the tool result would also not contain the function name.

options.text: Claude watched the terminal output directly while Bash ran, because built-in tools pass their results to the model without any step in the loop.
options.reason: The guide's loop lifecycle has the loop execute the requested tool and return the result for the next iteration. Claude sees only what the loop adds to the conversation.
